facts.fact: Rabbits eat grass, leaves, and other plants. Their front teeth never stop growing, so they chew tough plants to wear the teeth down.
facts.hook: a pet rabbit that only wants cake, and its teeth keep getting longer

facts.fact: A frog starts life as a tadpole that lives in water and breathes with gills like a fish. Later it grows legs and can hop onto land.
facts.hook: a tadpole who wants to join the frogs on land before it has legs

facts.fact: A snail's shell is part of its body, so a snail can never leave its shell or move into a different one.
facts.hook: a child who tries to give a snail a bigger, fancier shell

facts.fact: Bees make honey from nectar, the sweet juice they drink from flowers and carry back to their hive.
facts.hook: a bear who thinks honey comes from the store, not from flowers

facts.fact: Owls sleep during the day and hunt at night. Their feathers are so soft that they can fly almost without a sound.
facts.hook: a child who invites an owl to a picnic at noon

facts.fact: A duck spreads oil from its own body over its feathers, so water rolls off and the duck stays dry while it swims.
facts.hook: a soaking-wet child who wonders why the duck is dry

facts.fact: An elephant sucks water up into its trunk, then squirts the water into its mouth to drink. It does not drink through the trunk like a straw.
facts.hook: a child who tries to drink through a hose like an elephant

facts.fact: A newborn kangaroo is about the size of a jellybean. It crawls into its mother's pouch and grows there for months.
facts.hook: a child at the zoo looking for the big baby kangaroo

facts.fact: Spiders have eight legs, but insects like ants, bees, and beetles have six. So a spider is not an insect.
facts.hook: a child who counts legs to find out what kind of bug it is

facts.fact: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. They use their wings like flippers to zoom through the water.
facts.hook: a child who tries to teach a penguin to fly

facts.fact: Many birds fly to warmer places when winter is coming and fly back in the spring.
facts.hook: a child who thinks the birds are lost and wants to bring them home

facts.fact: A seed needs water and warmth to sprout. The root grows down first, then the green shoot grows up toward the light.
facts.hook: a child who plants a seed upside down and worries it will grow the wrong way

facts.fact: Plants make their own food from sunlight. A plant kept in a dark closet turns pale and floppy.
facts.hook: a child who hides a plant in the closet to keep it safe

facts.fact: A cloud is made of tiny drops of water floating in the air. When the drops join up and get too heavy, they fall as rain.
facts.hook: a child who tries to catch a cloud in a jar

facts.fact: To see a rainbow, the sun must be behind you and the rain in front of you. Sunlight goes through the raindrops and splits into colors.
facts.hook: a child who runs toward the sun looking for the rainbow

facts.fact: Snow is frozen water. A snowball brought into a warm house melts into a puddle.
facts.hook: a child who saves a snowball in a drawer for summer

facts.fact: The sun looks small because it is very far away. It is really much, much bigger than the whole Earth.
facts.hook: a child who is sure the sun is the size of a ball

facts.fact: The moon does not make its own light. It looks bright because sunlight bounces off it.
facts.hook: a child who tries to find the moon's light switch

facts.fact: Some trees drop all their leaves in the fall and grow new ones in the spring. Pine trees keep their needles all year.
facts.hook: a child who thinks the bare tree in the yard has died

facts.fact: Lightning and thunder happen at the same time, but you see the flash before you hear the boom, because light travels faster than sound.
facts.hook: a child who counts between the flash and the boom

facts.fact: Each fluffy bit of a dandelion puff is a seed with a tiny parachute. The wind can carry the seed far away to grow somewhere new.
facts.hook: a child who blows a dandelion and worries where the seeds went

facts.fact: Wind is air that is moving. You cannot see the wind, but you can see what it pushes, like leaves, flags, and kites.
facts.hook: a child who tries to catch the wind in a bag

facts.fact: A puddle disappears on a warm day because the water slowly turns into a gas called water vapor and floats up into the air.
facts.hook: a child who guards a puddle so nobody can take it

facts.fact: Every morning the sun comes up on the east side of the sky, and every evening it goes down on the west side.
facts.hook: a child who waits for the sunset at the wrong window

facts.fact: Fog is a cloud that sits on the ground. Walking through fog means walking through a cloud.
facts.hook: a child who wants to touch a cloud and finally can on a foggy morning

facts.fact: A tree grows one new ring inside its trunk each year. You can count the rings on a cut stump to find out how old the tree was.
facts.hook: a child who counts stump rings to see if the tree was older than grandma

facts.fact: Your heart is a pump about the size of your fist. It beats faster when you run so it can send more blood to your legs.
facts.hook: a child who feels their heart thumping after a race and worries

facts.fact: Hair and fingernails keep growing all the time. Cutting them does not hurt because the parts you cut are not alive.
facts.hook: a child who is scared a haircut will hurt

facts.fact: Your nose does a lot of your tasting. When your nose is stuffed up from a cold, food tastes bland because you cannot smell it.
facts.hook: a child with a cold who thinks the soup is broken

facts.fact: Cutting an onion lets out a gas that stings your eyes, so your eyes make tears to wash it away, even if you are not sad.
facts.hook: a child who thinks dad is crying because he is sad

facts.fact: You blink about fifteen times every minute to keep your eyes wet, and you usually do not notice.
facts.hook: a staring contest where nobody can win

facts.fact: Spinning around makes you dizzy because liquid inside your ears keeps swirling for a little while after you stop.
facts.hook: a child who spins in circles and then cannot walk straight

facts.fact: Children have twenty first teeth. Starting around age six, the first teeth fall out one by one and bigger teeth grow in.
facts.hook: a four-year-old who wants a tooth to fall out right now

facts.fact: You are a tiny bit taller in the morning than at night. The soft pads between the bones in your back get squished during the day.
facts.hook: a child who measures against the wall at bedtime and again at breakfast

facts.fact: A sneeze blasts air out of your nose very fast to blow out dust or anything that tickles inside.
facts.hook: a child who sniffs pepper to see what happens

facts.fact: Your skin has tiny holes that let out sweat. As the sweat dries, it cools you down.
facts.hook: a child who thinks sweating means something is wrong

facts.fact: A scab is dried blood that makes a lid over a cut. Under the lid, new skin grows.
facts.hook: a child who wants to peel off a scab to see what is under it

facts.fact: Sound is air wiggling. The wiggles reach a thin skin inside your ear, called the eardrum, and make it shake, and that is how you hear.
facts.hook: a child who feels a drum shake and wonders if ears do the same

facts.fact: Your tummy growls when it is empty. It squeezes and moves air around inside, and the air makes the noise.
facts.hook: a child whose tummy growls during quiet time

facts.fact: The black dot in the middle of your eye is a hole called the pupil. It gets bigger in the dark to let in more light and smaller in bright light.
facts.hook: two children checking each other's eyes with a flashlight

facts.fact: The tiny lines on your fingertips are your fingerprints. No two people have the same fingerprints, not even twins.
facts.hook: a mystery about who touched the frosting

facts.fact: When you count a group of things, the last number you say tells how many there are. You get the same answer no matter which one you count first.
facts.hook: a child who counts the cookies from both ends to check

facts.fact: A triangle has three straight sides and three corners. A square has four sides that are all the same length and four corners.
facts.hook: a child sorting crackers into triangles and squares

facts.fact: A circle has no corners, so a round wheel rolls smoothly. A block with corners bumps along and stops.
facts.hook: a wagon with square wheels that will not roll

facts.fact: If you share six cookies fairly between two friends, each friend gets three cookies.
facts.hook: two friends who argue until they count out the cookies

facts.fact: Zero means none at all. If you have zero apples, your basket is empty.
facts.hook: a child looking everywhere for the zero apples

facts.fact: A tall thin glass and a short wide glass can hold the same amount of juice, even though the tall one looks like more.
facts.hook: two siblings who each want the glass with more juice

facts.fact: The same buttons can be sorted more than one way, such as by color or by size. Both ways are right.
facts.hook: two children who sort the same buttons differently and both think they won

facts.fact: A pattern repeats the same way over and over, like red, blue, red, blue. Once you know the pattern, you can say what comes next.
facts.hook: a child stringing beads who runs out of blue ones

facts.fact: Half means two pieces that are exactly the same size. If one piece is bigger, it is not half.
facts.hook: a child who cuts a cookie in half but not fairly

facts.fact: To see which of two sticks is longer, line up one end of each stick. A stick that starts farther ahead can look longer when it is not.
facts.hook: a child who thinks their stick is longer until they line them up

facts.fact: You can measure how long something is by counting how many same-sized things fit along it, like blocks or shoes.
facts.hook: a child measuring the table in shoes

facts.fact: A cube has six flat square faces. A die is a cube, with a different number of dots on each face.
facts.hook: a child who tries to count all the sides of a die

facts.fact: Bigger does not always mean heavier. A big balloon weighs less than a small rock.
facts.hook: a child who thinks the biggest present must be the heaviest

facts.fact: There is no biggest number. Whatever number you say, you can always add one more.
facts.hook: a child who claims to know the biggest number

facts.fact: A zipper has two rows of tiny teeth. The slider locks the teeth together as you pull it up, and if one tooth is bent, the zipper gets stuck.
facts.hook: a child stuck in a coat with a broken zipper

facts.fact: A magnet sticks to things made of iron or steel, like a paper clip or a fridge door. It does not stick to wood, plastic, or glass.
facts.hook: a child who tries to hang a drawing on a wooden door with a magnet

facts.fact: A fridge keeps food cold by pulling heat out of the inside and pushing it out the back. That is why the back of a fridge feels warm.
facts.hook: a child who feels the warm fridge and thinks it is broken

facts.fact: A seesaw is a lever. A small person sitting far from the middle can lift a big person sitting close to the middle.
facts.hook: a small child who lifts dad on the seesaw

facts.fact: Water alone slides off grease. Soap grabs onto grease and lets the water carry it away, so greasy hands need soap.
facts.hook: a child who washes with water only and still has sticky hands

facts.fact: A wagon moves easily because its wheels turn on a rod called an axle. Dragging the same load without wheels is much harder.
facts.hook: a child moving a pile of rocks with and without a wagon

facts.fact: Glass is made from sand. The sand is heated until it melts into a gooey liquid, shaped, and then cooled until it is hard.
facts.hook: a child at the beach who wonders if sand could become a window

facts.fact: Paper is made from trees. The wood is chopped into tiny bits, mixed with water into mush, pressed flat, and dried.
facts.hook: a child who thanks a tree for the drawing paper

facts.fact: Electricity only flows when the path is complete. A light switch opens a gap in the wire to turn the light off and closes it to turn the light on.
facts.hook: a child with a flashlight that will not work because a wire is loose

facts.fact: In a glass thermometer, the liquid inside takes up more room when it warms up, so it climbs higher in the tube.
facts.hook: a child who warms a thermometer in their hands to make it climb

facts.fact: Bread dough rises because yeast, a tiny living thing, eats sugar in the dough and makes bubbles of gas.
facts.hook: a child who watches dough grow and thinks it is alive

facts.fact: A key opens a lock because its bumps push tiny pins inside to exactly the right heights. A different key pushes them to the wrong heights.
facts.hook: a child who tries every key on the ring

facts.fact: Wool comes from sheep. The sheep get a haircut, and the wool is washed, spun into yarn, and knitted into sweaters.
facts.hook: a child who worries a freshly shorn sheep will be cold

facts.fact: When you push a toilet handle, water rushes from the tank into the bowl. The rushing water pulls everything down the pipe.
facts.hook: a child who wonders where the water goes

facts.fact: Water cannot soak into plastic, so it rolls off a raincoat. Cotton soaks water up, so a cotton sweater gets heavy and wet.
facts.hook: a child who picks a sweater instead of a raincoat

facts.fact: A fire truck's hose connects to a hydrant on the street. The hydrant is connected to big water pipes under the ground.
facts.hook: a child who wonders how the fire truck carries enough water

facts.fact: A letter dropped in a mailbox is picked up by a mail carrier, sorted at a big building, and then delivered to the address written on it.
facts.hook: a child who mails a letter to grandma without writing the address

facts.fact: Farmers grow wheat, which is ground into flour at a mill. A baker mixes the flour with water and yeast to make bread.
facts.hook: a child who thinks bread grows on trees

facts.fact: A dentist uses a tiny mirror on a stick to see the backs of your teeth, where you cannot see them yourself.
facts.hook: a child who is sure the back teeth are already clean

facts.fact: At a store, you trade money for things. The store uses that money to buy more things to sell and to pay the people who work there.
facts.hook: a child who thinks the store gives things away

facts.fact: A stop sign has eight sides. No other road sign has that shape, so drivers know it is a stop sign even from behind.
facts.hook: a child who counts the sides of every sign on the walk to school

facts.fact: Tap water comes from a river, lake, or well. It is cleaned at a water plant before it travels through pipes to your house.
facts.hook: a child who thinks the tap makes the water

facts.fact: A doctor listens to your heart and breathing with a stethoscope. The sound travels up the tubes to the doctor's ears.
facts.hook: a child who tries the stethoscope on a teddy bear

facts.fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
facts.hook: a child who wants to keep the library book forever

facts.fact: Bakers start work very early, often before the sun comes up, so the bread is ready when the shop opens.
facts.hook: a child who wakes up early to see the bread being made

facts.fact: A lighthouse shines a bright light at night so ships know where the rocky shore is and can steer away from it.
facts.hook: a child who thinks the lighthouse is calling the ships in

facts.fact: When a group needs to pick one thing, people can vote. Each person picks once, and the choice with the most votes wins.
facts.hook: a class voting on a name for the pet fish
